title: Lightweight adaptive kernel sampling + shadow-map telemetry for low-overhead runtime profiling
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Implement a low-overhead runtime telemetry mechanism that provides per-kernel latency distributions and request-level attribution with sub-ms overhead. The design introduces: (1) an adaptive sampler that switches between probabilistic sampling and hot-path ring-buffer capture for microsecond kernels, (2) a lightweight shadow-map that correlates GPU exec IDs/stream tokens to request IDs without touching production request paths, and (3) compact histogram storage and OTLP export with optional coalesced spans for backend storage efficiency.
motivation: Current kernel telemetry either (a) samples too coarsely and misses short but frequent kernels, or (b) generates too much trace noise when enabled across all production hosts. We need a hybrid approach that surfaces tail and hot-path regressions while keeping cost and CPU/GPU overhead low so it can be enabled in Dedicated and Private fleets by default.
design_summary: 1) Sampling: probabilistic base sampling (1-2%) plus an adaptive hot-path ring buffer per worker that captures the most recent N kernel execs for each stream when frequency thresholds exceed a configured rate. 2) Shadow-map: a lock-free ring that pairs transient GPU exec handles (exec_id, stream_id) to lightweight request fingerprints (8B hash) produced by the scheduler. This map is read by the telemetry thread to stitch kernel metrics back to request fingerprints. 3) Compact payload: per-exec entry records kernel_name, exec_fingerprint, duration_us, queued_latency_us, kernel_args_hash (optional), and a small flags byte. Exporter coalesces adjacent entries with the same fingerprint into a single span with per-kernel child annotations or histogram attachment. 4) Integration: OTLP/gRPC exporter to our trace pipeline with config toggles for full spans vs. histogram-only export.
tradeoffs_decisions:
- Choosing an 8-byte request fingerprint trades exact request idability for a low-memory, low-copy correlate. Acceptable because we can map fingerprints back via optional sampled full-request traces.
- Ring buffer size default set to 256 entries per stream to balance memory vs visibility; we will make this dynamic per-host memory class.
- Coalescing spans reduces backend storage cost but makes immediate per-kernel timeline reconstruction harder. We include a debug mode that disables coalescing for targeted investigation.
- We avoid instrumenting deep model internals (activations) to keep telemetry safe for PII-sensitive deployments; kernel args are hashed when enabled.
acceptance_criteria:
- End-to-end telemetry with <1% CPU overhead on standard worker profile (64-vCPU host) when enabled in default mode.
- Measured p50/p95/p99 kernel latency histograms match profiler ground truth within 10% across synthetic workloads.
- Ability to correlate at least 90% of hot-path kernel execs to a sampled request fingerprint in stress tests.
- Dashboard in Console showing per-model/per-instance kernel histogram heatmaps and an example trace that maps back to a request fingerprint.
- Feature flags to enable ring-buffer capture and to toggle coalescing per fleet.
implementation_plan:
- Week 1: implement ring buffer and shadow-map APIs in runtime core (unsafe-free, lockless, bounded memory).
- Week 2: implement adaptive sampler and exporter that emits compact OTLP protos and histogram attachments.
- Week 3: add coalescing logic and debug mode; integration tests and end-to-end traces in staging.
- Week 4: benchmark suite across representative models (short-shot completion models, long-context chat) and iterate thresholds.
- Week 5: rollout on canary fleet, observe telemetry costs, then ramp to Dedicated and Private clusters.
tasks: runtime: add per-stream ring buffer and lightweight exec record (ENG-110052-1)
scheduler: emit 8B request fingerprint and attach exec token to launch calls (ENG-110052-2)
telemetry: OTLP exporter and coalescing logic (ENG-110052-3)
console: histogram heatmap panel and trace drilldown (ENG-110052-4)
qa: perf regression tests and accuracy validation (ENG-110052-5)
risks:
- Overhead may exceed target on small hosts; mitigation: dynamic sampling throttles and host memory classes.
- Hash collisions cause false attribution; mitigation: fall back to sampled full traces when collisions suspected.
- Backend storage growth if coalescing disabled; mitigation: retention and aggregation policies in ingestion pipeline.
benchmarks_plan: Run three synthetic workloads: tiny-token model (tokens<32) at high QPS, medium-token chat (avg 128), and long-generation (avg 512). Measure: CPU impact, GPU stall contribution, OTLP payload size, histogram fidelity vs. offline profiler. Target payload <= 40KB/min per host in default config.
observability_goals: Expose metrics: sampled_exec_rate, ring_buffer_fill_ratio, stitched_percentage, exporter_latency_ms, avg_payload_bytes. Emit logs at debug-only level for shadow-map evictions and collision counts.
security_privacy_notes: No raw prompt text leaves the host as part of this telemetry. Kernel args are hashed and can be disabled. Fingerprints are 8B non-reversible hashes; full request ids are only exported in sampled full-traces when debug tracing enabled and under customer-approved telemetry settings.
rollout_steps: 1) Feature flag gated in runtime config. 2) Canary on internal dev fleet for 48h with alerting on CPU/regressions. 3) Enable on non-sensitive Dedicated clusters and monitor. 4) Offer as opt-in for Private customers via config. 5) Document on runbook and Console flags.

2026-02-28: Scheduler change landed to emit 8B fingerprint; added defensive incrementing to avoid duplicate exec tokens.
2026-03-05: Exporter draft emits OTLP spans with compressed histogram attachment; coalescing strategy prototype reduces payloads by ~6x on test workloads.
2026-03-11: Staging run uncovered ring buffer eviction pattern on high-cardinality streams; increased hot-path threshold and added per-host memory class config.
